Educated at Sherwood College, Nainital and the Prince of Wales Royal Military College, Dehradun, he was commissioned in February 1942 into the 8th Battalion, 19th Hyderabad Regiment (later 4 Kumaon). He served in Burma during the Arakan campaign and was mentioned in despatches. In October 1947, despite a fractured left arm in plaster from a hockey injury, he insisted on flying to Srinagar with his company. He was killed on 3 November 1947 at Badgam and became the first recipient of the Param Vir Chakra, gazetted on 21 June 1950.
soldiers.act_of_valor: On 3 November 1947, D Company of 4 Kumaon under Major Sharma was on a fighting patrol at Badgam, covering the approach to Srinagar airfield. Around 2:35 pm the company was attacked from three sides by an estimated 500–700 tribal raiders supported by mortars, and began taking heavy casualties. Sharma repeatedly crossed open ground under fire to direct his sections, laid out cloth strips to guide IAF aircraft onto targets, and, with his left hand in plaster, personally filled magazines for the light machine guns. A mortar shell landed on the ammunition beside him and killed him. His company held the position long enough to delay the raiders by about six hours, allowing reinforcements to secure Hum Hom and the airfield. One JCO and 20 other ranks of D Company died with him.

He continued engaging further tanks until his jeep was hit by enemy tank fire and he was killed. His official citation credits at least two tanks destroyed; regimental and other accounts credit more. His action contributed to the collapse of the Pakistani armoured thrust at Asal Uttar.
